transcript:
Header:
Date: 2025-09-17
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~58 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Diego (Redwood SE), Lena (Redwood SE), Tom (Redwood Partner Ops), Priya (Crestline Director Cloud Eng), Ethan (Crestline CTO), Samir (Crestline Security), Marta (Crestline PM)

Auto Summary (auto-generated, may be incomplete):
- Goal: align on marketplace listing requirements, packaging format, VPC/on-prem connector behaviors, and KMS compatibility for Crestline's planned private deployment trial.
- Action items: share packaging checklist, run perf baseline, schedule KMS deep dive.

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya: hey everyone thanks for joining, I think we, yeah we have most of the folks. quick intros, i'll keep it short. im maya from redwood, AE on the partner motion.
[00:10] Priya: hi this is priya, director of cloud eng at crestline, thanks for setting this up. we wanted to focus this call on the marketplace listing artifacts and onprem connector behaviors we saw in the doc.
[00:20] Diego: great, diego here, i'll lead the technical bits, especially around helm/operator, and the private deploy packaging.
[00:28] Ethan: ethan, cto. high level — timeline is end of q4 for a pilot, hope to confirm in next 3 weeks.
[00:36] Samir: samir here, security. i'll have the KMS and SSO questions.
[00:40] Marta: marta, product, i'll be owning verification and acceptance criteria.

[00:52] Maya: ok we'll go through the packaging checklist first, then the VPC/kms questions, then perf/quantization notes. hopefully wrap with explicit next steps.

[02:05] Diego: so on packaging, we recommend a helm chart + a small operator for lifecycle hooks — common pattern is chart under /charts/redwood-connector and values.yaml with: image, replicas, vpcNetwork, kmsKeyArn, storageClass. we have an example helm values in the partner repo: https://redwood.partners/example/helm-values (note: temporary link)
[02:35] Priya: when you say operator, is that required? our infra team prefers plain helm to avoid extra controllers.
[02:44] Lena: it's optional. operator only handles controlled rollouts and cache warmup (prefix cache) — if you want manual control you can run helm only, the operator gives easier canary and automatic KV cache seeding.
[03:02] Ethan: can you explain "KV cache seeding" quick?
[03:08] Diego: sure, it's basically pre-populating model key/value caches for common prefixes to reduce cold-start latency. think of it as warmup queries stored in persistent volume or memory depending on config. sometimes the transcript will render "kay vee" cache, haha.

[04:20] Samir: on the KMS side, our policy requires that customer-managed keys are used and that logs show envelope key operations. does redwood support BYOK with HSM-backed CMKs?
[04:33] Diego: yes — Redwood Private supports KMS integrations; we support AWS KMS, Azure Key Vault and KMIP-compatible HSMs in onprem. for BYOK we do envelope encryption and can surface audit logs to your SIEM. there are small caveats around operator perms and mount options.
[04:55] Priya: what does the operator need permission-wise? we prefer least-privilege.
[05:01] Diego: operator needs ability to read secrets, create k8s jobs for cache seeding, patch deployments for canary rollouts, and list/attach PVCs. for KMS operations only the runtime node role needs the envelope decrypt/encrypt, operator doesn't perform raw encrypt ops. we'll send a minimal IAM/role spec.

[07:12] Priya: ok that helps. on data residency — our legal team insists data never leaves our VPC. does marketplace listing force any egress to hosted redwood control plane?
[07:24] Tom: quick clar — our marketplace packaging supports a private control plane option. when you pick Private deployment via marketplace, control-plane calls can either be proxied over your VPC peering or run in a customer-managed control plane. in the latter case there is zero egress of payloads. docs: redwood.com/partners/private-deploy (note: link is illustrative)
[07:46] Ethan: so for pilot we can pick private with customer-managed control plane?
[07:50] Tom: yes, that is the pattern we typically recommend for regulated data. it increases ops overhead a bit but meets residency + audit needs.

[09:05] Marta: about the marketplace listing metadata, are there required artifacts for the store? like diagrams, test fixtures?
[09:13] Maya: yes required: architecture diagram (png/svg), helm chart tarball, values example, quickstart README, a small smoke test script, and a security checklist (SOC2 pointers). optional: a prebuilt quantized model bundle if you want to show cost/latency delta.
[09:40] Priya: can we host the helm chart in our own repo and point marketplace to it?
[09:45] Tom: yes the listing can point to an OCI registry or a partner tarball location — as long as the listing passes validation we can accept external hosting. the validation CI checks packaging and run smoke deploys in a sandbox.

[11:02] Diego: quick perf note — for retrieval-heavy workloads we recommend int8 quantization for the encoder model and a 4-bit for the decoder when available — this balances latency vs. output quality. results will vary. we usually provide guidance per model.
[11:20] Ethan: does redwood do quantization in the runtime, or do we need to ship a quantized artifact?
[11:27] Diego: both options: you can deliver a quantized model artifact, or use Redwood Optimize profiles that apply quantization at build-time in our packaging pipeline. when done at runtime there's some perf variability, so we usually test a pre-quantized artifact for enterprise pilots.

[12:35] Marta: what about networking — do we need specific firewall rules for the connector?
[12:40] Diego: minimal egress: package download (if using external chart registry), control plane health pings to a regional endpoint (or none if customer-managed), and optional telemetry to Redwood telemetry endpoint (can be disabled). we will share ip ranges and hostnames.

[14:50] Samir: audit logs — we need request-level logs for a 90 day retention and immutable storage. is that supported?
[14:58] Lena: yes. Private deployments can ship logs to your S3/GCS/Azure Blob with lifecycle rules. we also support append-only audit logs via our logging adapter that writes to your bucket with object lock configs. we'll share the adapter config.

[16:12] Ethan: about the acceptance criteria for the pilot — minimal SLO is 99.5% availability and p95 latency under 120ms for 512 token context in our internal tests, does that sound realistic?
[16:23] Diego: thats achievable on Dedicated or private with right instance sku and batching config. on smaller instances you may see higher p95. we can run a perf baseline against your staging workload to validate.

[17:10] Priya: what inputs do you need for the baseline?
[17:14] Diego: sample prompt set (10-20 representative prompts), QPS profile (peak and average), context length distribution, and whether responses should be streamed. we'll provide a small runner script that emits load and collects token-level latencies.

[19:05] Marta: do you have any templates for the acceptance test?
[19:09] Maya: yes we'll attach a 'pilot-acceptance-template.md' with pass/fail gates for latency, correctness (prompt set scoring), and security checks.

[20:30] Priya: about pricing on marketplace — we want to know how billing works when using private control plane and customer-managed infra.
[20:38] Tom: marketplace listing can surface estimated usage pricing but actual billing for private on your infra is typically a license + support fee model rather than per-token. we can share a ballpark. for the pilot we usually do a capped evaluation invoice.

[22:01] Ethan: any known gotchas when running the helm/chart in air-gapped clusters?
[22:06] Diego: main issues are image pulls and package dependencies — we provide an air-gap bundle (tar) with images and the chart, and an import script. the operator expects certain nodes with nvme for cache; we document fallback to PV if not present.

[24:10] Samir: on SSO we require SAML SSO + SCIM provisioning. supported?
[24:14] Maya: yes we support SAML + SCIM for RBAC mapping. for marketplace listing you include an SSO integration guide and we validate SAML federation flows during listing approval.

[26:00] Priya: is the marketplace listing approval a manual review? timeline?
[26:05] Tom: validation is CI-driven first, then a 2-3 business day manual review for enterprise checks. expect 5–10 business days end-to-end if there are no blockers.

[28:30] Marta: oc — will the listing expose a demo endpoint? we want to link to a self-serve demo in the listing.
[28:36] Maya: yes you can include a playbook link and a demo endpoint — but for private deployments the demo is usually behind access restrictions. for hosted demos we can host a lightweight sandbox.

[30:45] Diego: differences between Hosted and Dedicated for your use case: Hosted is easiest but tokens/data go through our hosted runtime; Dedicated gives isolated GPU pool (better predictable p95) and Private with customer control plane gives full data residency.

[33:10] Priya: our preference is private with customer-managed control plane. next question: telemetry — we need to control sampling rate and ensure no PII is sent.
[33:21] Lena: sampling controls exist; default telemetry is token-level anonymized metrics only, raw prompts are never sent unless you opt-in for debug. for the listing you should make it clear what is sent and give an opt-out flag.

[36:00] Ethan: competitors — we evaluated NimbusCloud and EdgeBridge. Nimbus had easier onboarding but higher per-token cost, EdgeBridge required more ops work. can redwood do a quick comparison matrix?
[36:13] Maya: yes we'll do a short competitor comparison tailored to your criteria (ops overhead, unit cost, privacy).

[38:20] Samir: on compliance pack — we need SOC2 type II artifacts, pen test summary, and any third-party attestations.
[38:28] Maya: we'll share our security pack and SOC2 cert; we'll also include our recommended scoping doc for the pen test.

[40:15] Marta: about the rollout plan in the helm values, can we configure canary percent and auto-fallback?
[40:21] Diego: yes the operator supports canary percentages, auto rollback on error rate, and automatic fallback to a lighter model variant if quality/regression is detected by our eval hooks.

[42:05] Priya: eval hooks — do you have an out-of-the-box eval harness?
[42:09] Diego: Redwood Optimize has eval harness templates; we can run prompt sets and track quality/regression and tie alerts to rollbacks.

[44:30] Maya: ok timebox — last 10 minutes for decisions and next steps.
[44:36] Ethan: decision: start with private customer-managed control plane in staging; we will validate perf and security and then list in the marketplace as a private offering.

[45:05] Maya: great. summary next steps: maya sends packaging checklist & helm sample, diego runs perf baseline, samir and diego schedule kms deep dive. priya will run the staging deploy and share logs.

[46:22] Priya: couple clarifications — will you provide sample values for PVC sizing and node SKUs?
[46:29] Diego: yes sample sizes based on model family — we'll include node flavor recs (e.g., a2-highmem variants) and PVC suggestions.

[48:00] Marta: can you also attach a minimal smoke test we can run (curl-based)?
[48:04] Lena: yes we'll include 'smoke.sh' and a small python runner.

[50:10] Ethan: ok thanks everyone, this was very helpful.
[50:14] Maya: thanks all, we'll follow up with the docs and the calendar invites for the KMS deep-dive.
[50:23] Samir: thanks.
[50:25] (call ends around 15:58 UTC)
